content: GPU floating point is close to but not exactly IEEE 754 (rounding mode/denormal/NaN handling can differ by vendor) -- but bit-exact repeatability IS achievable for a FIXED pipeline (same shader binary, same driver, same GPU, same execution schedule) because the same instruction sequence run the same way produces the same rounding every time; non-determinism enters via (a) unordered parallel reductions/atomics whose accumulation order can vary run-to-run (float addition is non-associative under IEEE 754), (b) MSAA resolve / blend ops with driver-internal reordering, (c) LOAD_OP_DONT_CARE reading stale/undefined memory. DETV-01/02's guards (VK_SAMPLE_COUNT_1_BIT always, explicit clears, no unordered-reduction shader math, fixed precision qualifiers) directly target the known non-associativity and undefined-read failure classes; this is architectural avoidance of nondeterminism sources, not a claim that Vulkan/GPUs are inherently IEEE-754-safe by default.
